5. [TRIGGER-NATIVE-CONTROLS] chips are native <button type=button> in a role=group; scheme classes come from eventTypeBadgeClass (one scheme, no duplication); label text on every chip.
6. New keys in all four locales; polyphony single-select pattern followed (multi-select noted as follow-up only if legacy showed it).
7. Tests: derivation, toggle, both sections, other grouping, disappearance reset, filtered-empty, collective switch, scheme classes, guards. pnpm test + pnpm check green.
tasks.commitBody:
Event type filter chips above the agenda: one native button per
event type present in the rendered agenda (recent and upcoming, across
the seasons the list spans) plus an explicit All chip, following the
polyphony.uk single-select pattern. Tapping a chip filters both agenda
sections to that type; tapping it again shows all. Free-text or empty
types group under the 'other' chip while their badges keep the raw
string. If the active type disappears from the list the filter resets
to all, and it resets on collective switch. Filtering happens at page
level so AgendaList stays filter-agnostic; a filtered result with no
rows shows a distinct message. Chips reuse the #211 badge scheme.

New keys agenda_filter_all, agenda_filter_group_label,
agenda_filter_empty in en/et/lv/uk.

Closes #214
